newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary to open new consulate in Romania next week. [CORRECTED 15:29 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Hungary to open new consulate in Romania next week. [CORRECTED 15:29 GMT]

text.p: Hungary is to open a new consulate in Romania next week in a gesture designed to show that the two countries' relations have not worsened as a result of Romania's failure to be admitted into NATO.

The new mission will open in a temporary building on July 16, in Cluj, in western Romania (correcting country), and will be officially inaugurated one week later, Hungary's foreign ministry said on Friday.
Ministry spokesman Gabor Horvath told Reuters the timing of the opening, just a week after NATO announced that Romania would not join Hungary in the first wave of enlargement, was significant.
"The new consulate is an important symbolic message regarding the strong improving relations between the two countries and both Hungary and Romania want to emphasise this," he said.

The two countries agreed earlier this year to open new provincial consulates in each other's country as part of a warming of ties following the signing of a friendship treaty and the election of President Emil Constantinescu last November.
Better ties between Bucharest and Budapest helped put Romania in the running for the first group of new countries invited to become members of NATO at the Madrid summit earlier this week.

However the alliance only invited Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic to form the first wave of expansion but mentioned Romania, along with Slovenia, as being especially well placed to join in the second group to be considered in 1999.
U.S. President Bill Clinton is in Romania on Friday to encourage the Balkan country to pursue reforms and persist with its bid for NATO membership.
Horvath said Hungary had decided to open the new mission in a temporary office rather than wait until a suitable permanent building had been found.

"We didn't want to wait until we had the new building because this is a good time symbolically and there is a lot of demand in the summer from tourists and ethnic Hungarians from the region," he said.
Hungarian Foreign Minister Laszlo Kovacs will attend the official opening along with his Romanian counterpart, Adrian Severin, Horvath added.
Romania's Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu closed Hungary's consulate in Cluj in 1977.

The move to shut down the mission, in the heart of Transylvania, where most of Romania's 1.4 million strong ethnic Hungarian community lives, provoked Budapest to do the same to the Romanian representation in the eastern Hungarian town of Debrecen soon afterwards.

Romania will later this year open a consulate in the south eastern Hungarian town of Szeged while further missions are planned for the western Hungarian city of Gyor and the Romanian Black Sea port of Constanta.
